description: Instructions hidden in a tool's description or schema. The model reads them; the user rarely does.
A poisoned description that changes how the agent uses a different, trusted tool, without the poisoned tool ever being called.
A server or package that changes its definitions or code after it was approved, so an earlier review no longer holds.
The SHA-256 fingerprint of an approved tool definition (canonical JSON). Any change withholds the tool until a human re-approves it.
A serialization with keys sorted at every depth and no whitespace, so equal definitions always hash the same.
Code points U+E0000 to U+E007F that render as nothing but carry text a model can read.
Registering package names that models tend to hallucinate, so an agent that installs its own suggestion installs malware.
